name: Charred lemongrass chicken with edamame rice — low-sodium, optimized

source.author: Optimized version of lemongrass_chicken_edamame_rice
source.notes: Dual-lens-optimized version of lemongrass_chicken_edamame_rice, adopted per user request. Changes: fish sauce cut from ¼ cup (4 tbsp) to 2½ tbsp — the single biggest sodium lever; chicken broth for the rice swapped to a low-sodium version; added salt reduced to a small pinch (~¼ tsp, to taste) instead of a looser 'to taste' default. Everything else identical (chicken thighs, garlic, shallot, lemongrass, lime, brown sugar, dark soy sauce, basmati rice, edamame, parsley, togarashi, same method). As with the base recipe, the source caption text itself described a mismatched 'steak salad' — this entry follows the actual chicken + rice ingredients/method, same as the base. Sodium remains a wide-range estimate since marinade consumption during broiling/air-frying is approximate. Estimate.

ingredients.note: cut from the base recipe's ¼ cup (4 tbsp) — the biggest sodium lever

ingredients.item: low-sodium chicken broth (for cooking the rice)

ingredients.qty: a small pinch (~¼ tsp), to taste

steps: Blend the garlic, shallot, lemongrass, lime juice, brown sugar, fish sauce, soy sauce and water until smooth.
Pour most of it over the chicken and marinate; reserve a little clean marinade to brush on at the end.
Cook the rice per package instructions, substituting low-sodium chicken broth for the water.
Fold the cooked rice with the edamame, parsley and togarashi; season with just a small pinch of salt, tasting first.
Broil or air-fry the chicken on high heat until charred and cooked through, brushing with the reserved marinade.
Serve the chicken over the edamame rice.

batch_totals.note: Whole dish (6 servings), optimized. Vs the base recipe (per serving ~549 kcal / 42 g protein / ~1,869 mg sodium): nearly identical protein, fiber and calories, but sodium drops by roughly a third (~1,241 mg/serving vs ~1,869 mg) from the smaller fish sauce amount, low-sodium broth, and lighter added salt. Still on the higher side — fish sauce and dark soy together remain real contributors — but a meaningful improvement.

him.verdict: Keeps everything that made the base recipe good — ~41.8 g protein and ~4.2 g fiber per serving, with edamame doing real nutritional work alongside the chicken and rice — while cutting sodium by roughly a third. It's still not a low-sodium dish (fish sauce and dark soy are both inherently salty, and this is a rice bowl with a lot of volume), but it's a meaningfully better version of a dish you'll presumably eat regularly in the rotation.
flags: ~41.8 g protein / 547 kcal, with edamame contributing real protein + fiber
sodium down ~33% vs the base recipe (~1,241 mg/serving vs ~1,869 mg)
still moderately high sodium — fish sauce + dark soy are inherently salty ingredients
substantial carbs (~71 g/serving) from rice — reasonable for a dinner, less so for a lighter meal
moderate fat (~10 g), broiled/air-fried not deep-fried
suggested_mods: Great as the regular rotation version; the base recipe isn't needed once this is in place
If sodium is still a concern on a given day, a smaller rice portion is the easiest lever left (the sauce ingredients are already at a reasonable minimum for flavor)

her_preconception.verdict: Same genuine folate + fiber contribution from the edamame, same solid protein from the chicken, now with meaningfully less sodium. Fully cooked, no safety flags. A good regular option for her with the sodium reduction factored in.
prenatal_highlights: folate + fiber from edamame — a real plant source of her top nutrient
lower sodium than the base version
suggested_mods: Pair with a vitamin-C side (citrus, pepper) if eating this often, to round things out further

adopted_note: Adopted 2026-10-24 as the low-sodium optimized version of the lemongrass chicken with edamame rice (supersedes lemongrass_chicken_edamame_rice for actual use). Per serving (of 6, ~310 g): ~547 kcal, 41.8 g protein, 4.2 g fiber, ~1,241 mg sodium. him 8 / her 7. Standing spec: fish sauce cut to 2½ tbsp (from ¼ cup), low-sodium chicken broth for the rice, salt reduced to a small pinch to taste. Still a moderately high-sodium dish by nature of fish sauce + dark soy — this is the leanest-sodium version while keeping the flavor profile.
cooking_guide: Blend the marinade until fully smooth — lemongrass is fibrous, and leaving it chunky means unpleasant woody bits in the finished sauce.
Reserve some unused (never touched raw chicken) marinade before adding the rest to the chicken, so you have a clean portion to brush on at the end without any food-safety concern.
Pat the chicken thighs reasonably dry before marinating and again before broiling/air-frying — too much surface liquid stops you from getting a real char.
Cook the rice in low-sodium broth instead of water for savory depth without piling on extra salt.
Fold in the edamame, parsley and togarashi AFTER the rice is cooked and off the heat — keeps the edamame's color and the parsley fresh.
Taste the finished rice BEFORE adding the pinch of salt — the broth and togarashi may already be enough.
Broil or air-fry on genuinely high heat and don't walk away — you want char, not just cooked-through.
Brush with the reserved clean marinade in the last minute or two for a glossy, flavorful finish.
